data.reasoning: The package consists of a standard PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO for a Rust application. The PKGBUILD downloads a pinned source tarball from the official GitHub repository with a valid SHA256 checksum. The build steps are standard cargo commands. There are no malicious injections, dynamic code execution in the global scope, or suspicious network activity. The disagreement was solely caused by an API error in the Qwen model when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD.
data.disagreement_analysis: The Qwen model returned an inconclusive verdict because it encountered an HTTP 400 error when trying to audit the PKGBUILD file. The DeepSeek model successfully audited the PKGBUILD and correctly identified it as a safe, standard Rust packaging script. The disagreement is an artifact of a tool failure, not a difference in security analysis.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to audit the PKGBUILD file due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in an incomplete assessment.
learnings: The orchestration layer should implement retry logic for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400) on critical files (PKGBUILD) before marking a file or package as inconclusive.
When multiple models are used, partial failures in one model should be overridden by complete, successful audits from other models if they cover the same critical files.
